title.narrative: Providing health, educational and social care for conjoined twins

description.narrative: Ensuring a safe and complete physical, psychological and social recovery for conjoined twins according to professional scientific standards, and meeting their needs based on their health conditions. Developing the project's information and data management system and linking it to an integrated electronic system (database - information bank). Developing their educational and social skills by providing educational and rehabilitation programs and including them in primary and university education stages, to enable them to grow and develop naturally, enabling them to achieve independence and effective participation in society, contributing to preserving their dignity and ensuring their access to their human rights in all fields. Raising family and community awareness about the importance of supporting this group of children and contributing to enhancing their quality of life.

Regular medical follow-up and periodic examinations to ensure the recovery of children and prevent any health complications, providing all medicines, medical supplies and consumables, installing prosthetic limbs with the provision of rehabilitation therapy services (functional-physical), providing a suitable educational environment by providing educational tools that suit their physical needs, such as specialized chairs, special facilities for people with disabilities and the use of assistive tools and technology, such as interactive boards or writing and learning aids, providing educational grants or partial coverage of tuition fees for the most vulnerable families, and allocating individual educational plans, providing special means of transportation or facilities for easy and safe access to school and universities, providing psychological support services for conjoined twins and their families, providing secondary and tertiary health care services, educational and social services immediately and under the direction of the King Salman Center for Relief and Humanitarian Action and providing supporting documents for that to benefit a number of (60) conjoined twins

The project will be based on the principle of enabling access to health, educational and social services for conjoined twins in their countries and places of residence according to international standards and their health, educational and social needs, free of charge, and linking the services provided to an information and technical system (database - information bank) that ensures sustainable follow-up for them. This phase of the program represents a qualitative development to ensure the enhancement and continuity of providing services to them.
